# Riverside Community Midwives

## Helping your midwife find you

**A page for your welcome pack, your fridge, and the Riverside Facebook group**

Hello, and welcome. Our manager Deb asked me to write this page because I’m the midwife who always gets lost. So this comes from experience.

This isn’t a list of rules, and it isn’t a telling off. It’s just a few simple things that help us get to you quickly, calmly, and with our arms still working – especially at 3am when baby is coming.

### First things first: when we can come to you

Home birth cover starts from 37 weeks. Before 37 weeks, you will need to have your baby in hospital. We do tell everyone this at booking, but there is a lot to remember, so don’t worry if it has gone out of your head. If labour starts before 37 weeks, call the birth line and we will tell you what to do.

### When labour starts: who to call

Phone the **Riverside Birth Line** when labour starts. Please don’t phone my personal mobile, or message me on Facebook. The birth line goes straight to whoever is on call, so you will get the right midwife at the right time.

Write the number here and save it in your phone now:

**Riverside Birth Line: ______________________________**

If you are not sure whether labour has started, call the line anyway and speak to the midwife on call. We would much rather hear from you than have you sitting at home wondering.

### Help us park – and keep our arms working

Two midwives come to a home birth, usually in separate cars. If you can, please keep two parking spaces free close to your door.

We carry a lot: gas and air cylinders, the big bag, and sometimes the pool kit. Our arms are tired before we even get in. So if you see us coming, a clear space near the door is a beautiful thing.

If you live in a permit zone – around Anfield and Kensington especially – it’s worth asking the council about visitor permits before your due date, or having them ready on the dashboard. We have had parking tickets before, and nobody wants to start a birthday with a fine.

### Help us find your door

A visible house number or name makes a big difference. At night, please put the porch light on. Dark streets in winter all look the same, and I have driven past the right house more than once.

If you live in a flat, tell us the building name, which entrance, which floor, and whether the buzzer works. In one block of flats in Everton, flat 14 was not near flat 13 – it was in a different building. The dad ended up waving a tea towel out of the window. It worked, but only after 20 minutes of me going round and round.

If your house has a name but no number, like “Rosemary Cottage” in a street of terraces, tell us exactly what it is near. My sat nav once took me to a chip shop.

One family put balloons on their gate like it was a party. Best idea ever. I found it straight away. A ribbon, a sign, or a balloon is not silly – it is genuinely helpful.

The what3words app is good for this, or just send a pin on WhatsApp to the birth line phone. If you send a pin, send it to the birth line, not to my personal phone.

I once walked into the wrong house because the door was open. A lovely old man gave me a Jammie Dodger anyway. Lovely for me, not so good for the family waiting. So please make sure we know which door is yours.

### Pets, stairs and the path in

Please put pets in another room before we arrive. I love dogs – I really do – but not during pushing. One staffie called Pippin loved me a bit too much and jumped up on every visit. I nearly dropped the Entonox. Pippin was lovely. Pippin was also a lot.

Please clear the stairs and hallway as much as you can. No shoes in the way, no washing basket, no Lego. Lego is a special enemy of midwives at 3am. We are not coming to inspect your house. We just need a safe path from the door to you.

### Stick this bit on the fridge

- [ ] I have saved the Riverside Birth Line in my phone.
- [ ] I know to call the birth line when labour starts, not my midwife’s personal mobile.
- [ ] I know home birth cover starts from 37 weeks.
- [ ] I have kept two parking spaces free if possible.
- [ ] I have visitor permits ready if I live in a permit zone.
- [ ] My house number or name is easy to see.
- [ ] My porch light is on at night.
- [ ] I have sent a WhatsApp pin or what3words if my house is tricky to find.
- [ ] Pets are in another room.
- [ ] The hall and stairs are clear.
- [ ] I have something on the gate if my house is hidden.
- [ ] My phone is charged.

### A last word

In the Philippines, where I’m from, we say the midwife is like family. That’s how we want you to feel. We are not coming to inspect your house or tell you off. We are coming as friends who want to help you meet your baby safely.

We’ll see you soon.

**Riverside Community Midwives**
